text: A boundary/initial value problem is well-posed in the sense of Hadamard if a solution exists, is unique, and:
choices: can be written in closed form
is independent of the boundary conditions
explanation: Hadamard's third requirement is continuous dependence on the data (stability): small changes in the initial or boundary data produce small changes in the solution. Closed-form solvability is irrelevant, and the solution generally does depend on the boundary conditions.
